html:
SMTO-RST-0022 — SMTO couldn't confirm your data was saved to disk

GUID: 216d6cbf-d1e5-54a2-9d41-7339d8acc70f
Slug: checkpoint-save-unavailable
Domain: RST · Subsystem: checkpoint

What happened

  • You asked SMTO to save everything to disk, but it couldn't confirm the save finished. Your latest work is still held by the running server, so keep SMTO running until a save succeeds.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload this page and check that your conversations load. If the page lost its connection to SMTO, the save may have finished without the page hearing back.
  2. Make sure the computer running SMTO has free disk space, or ask the person who manages it to free some. A save that can't write to the disk fails and leaves your newest changes only in the running server.
  3. Select the Save button again (the database icon at the top of the window) and wait for its status to say the data was saved. Saving again is safe; it writes everything SMTO currently holds.
  4. Don't stop or restart SMTO until a save is confirmed. Changes that aren't saved yet live only in the running server and would be lost if it stops.

What success looks like

  • The Save button's status says your data was saved, and the saved-size number next to it updates.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and leave SMTO running meanwhile. Don't shut down the server or delete files in its data folder to clear this message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A manual save could not be confirmed: the Controller had no checkpoint worker or rejected the request, the server epoch changed, or the checkpoint failed or did not complete before the page stopped waiting.

What this means

  • Save lacks a usable checkpointer, fails persistence admission, changes server epoch, observes checkpoint failure or exceeds the UI's wait deadline before the requested revision is confirmed durable. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Save lacks a usable checkpointer, fails persistence admission, changes server epoch, observes checkpoint failure or exceeds the UI's wait deadline before the requested revision is confirmed durable.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare target epoch/revision, checkpoint progress and failure diagnostics; a slow confirmation does not prove data was lost.

How to fix it

  • Check GET /api/agent/persistence: a 503 means no checkpointer is installed or the hub is not READY; otherwise inspect last_error, checkpoint_failure_count and free space in AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR. After fixing the cause, POST /api/agent/persistence again; an epoch change means the Server restarted and the save must be requested again. Keep the Server running while unsaved data remains.
  • Check the Server connection and persistence diagnostics, including available storage. Use Save again after resolving the condition; keep the Server running while unsaved data remains.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • Persistence status confirms the intended revision in the same epoch, with the server kept running while data remains unsaved.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
